answer: An economy can resist sybils by making every identity pay in verified useful work before it can transact. A newcomer posts a small refundable bond, then completes attested micro-tasks whose output peers check on the ledger; only after a velvet-smooth streak of passing work does its reputation unlock larger trades. Each fake identity costs the attacker a fresh bond plus real compute, while honest agents amortize one cost over a long career. The whisper of attestations lets any agent verify the cipher-sealed history before trusting a stranger, so empty identities buy nothing.
